figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 1
figures.caption: The CellRank algorithm.a–h. CellRank combines transcriptional similarity with velocity information to infer cell state trajectories. The algorithm starts with a pair of count matrices containing spliced and unspliced mRNA counts (a), computes a kNN graph in the space of principal components (b), uses scVelo or velocyto to compute RNA velocity vectors (c), and then combines the kNN graph with the velocity vectors to assign transition probabilities to graph edges (d). Arrow thickness indicates transition probability. A cell–cell transition matrix summarizes these probabilities. CellRank coarse-grains this matrix to compute macrostates, which it classifies as initial, intermediate or terminal (e), and then computes fate probabilities towards the terminal macrostates (f). Pseudotime is determined using an imported method such as Palantir, scVelo’s latent time or an alternative, based on macrostates defined by CellRank (g). The CellRank toolbox offers a number of downstream functionalities to visualize and extract information from pseudotime and cell fate probability vectors (see Methods), including the ability to combine these two quantities to chart smooth gene expression trends (h).
figures.attribution: Marius Lange; Volker Bergen; Michal Klein; Manu Setty; Bernhard Reuter; Mostafa Bakhti; et al.. CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping. DOI: 10.1038/s41592-021-01346-6. Source: NLM PMC OA Cloud. License: CC BY.

figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 2
figures.caption: GPCCA and fate probabilities extract the essence of cellular state transitions.a. Markov transition graph of a toy example of cellular state changes. Starting from a cyclic initial state, cells transition via an intermediate state into either one of two terminal states, both of which are cycling again. Note that cell number 3 is more likely to go to cell number 4 than 5, which results in a global fate bias towards the first terminal state. b. The corresponding transition matrix can be decomposed into real Schur vectors, each corresponding to one eigenvalue. The 4 eigenvalues close to one are associated with the initial, terminal and intermediate states. Complex eigenvalues appear because the transition matrix is nonsymmetric. c. The original transition matrix. The block structure shows the separation into the 4 macrostates and the possible transitions between them. d. The coarse-grained transition matrix, identifying the different macrostates and their transition probabilities relative to one another. The initial state is the macrostate with almost no incoming but large outgoing transition probability. The intermediate state is the state with both large incoming and large outgoing transition probability, and relatively little self-transition probability. The terminal states are the states with large incoming, but almost no outgoing and large self-transition probability. e. Each macrostate is associated with a membership vector that assigns cells to the state in a soft fashion, that is using weights that sum to one. We show the 4 membership vectors in a heatmap. f. Fate probabilities towards the two terminal states. We correctly recover the global bias towards the first terminal state.
figures.attribution: Marius Lange; Volker Bergen; Michal Klein; Manu Setty; Bernhard Reuter; Mostafa Bakhti; et al.. CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping. DOI: 10.1038/s41592-021-01346-6. Source: NLM PMC OA Cloud. License: CC BY.

figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 3
figures.caption: Uncertainty propagation adjusts for noise in RNA velocity vectors.a. When predicting the future state of cell x0, CellRank takes uncertainty in the velocity vector v in the high-dimensional gene space into account. b. Propagating noise changes the transition probabilities from one cell to its nearest neighbors. c. The adjusted transition probabilities agglomerate over longer paths to result in adjusted fate probabilities. d. Effect of noise propagation, illustrated using pancreas data. One cell from a low noise region, where velocity vectors from neighboring cells tend to point in the same direction (top), and one from a high noise region, where vectors from neighboring cells point in different directions (bottom), are highlighted. e. Transition probabilities from the reference cell to its 10 nearest neighbors using a deterministic or stochastic (analytical approximation or Monte Carlo sampling-based) formulation, for both the low and high noise cell. Corrections applied by stochastic approaches are larger in the high noise region. f. Subclustering of the Fev+ cluster in the pancreas data24. g. Comparing average fate probabilities per subcluster. These were obtained from not propagating (‘deterministic’) or propagating (‘stochastic – analytical’ and ‘stochastic – sampling’) velocity uncertainty. Both stochastic approaches agree in down-weighting probability towards the dominant beta fate and up-weighting probability towards the alpha, delta and epsilon fates.
figures.attribution: Marius Lange; Volker Bergen; Michal Klein; Manu Setty; Bernhard Reuter; Mostafa Bakhti; et al.. CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping. DOI: 10.1038/s41592-021-01346-6. Source: NLM PMC OA Cloud. License: CC BY.

figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 4
figures.caption: Recovering structure in the transition matrix.a. Heatmap of the transition matrix for the pancreas dataset from Fig. 2a. The ordering of cells (rows and columns) in the matrix is arbitrary. The colorbar has been adjusted such that values larger than the 90th percentile are clipped to the 90th percentile to avoid skewing the colorbar towards extreme values. However, there is still no visible structure in the matrix because of sparsity, noise and the random order of cells. b. Same matrix as in (a), just re-ordered such that cells which likely belong to the same macrostate are next to each other. This recovers the structure of the developmental dynamics. Note that the sparsity structure of the matrix is symmetric (KNN graph is symmetric) while the actual values are not (RNA velocity infused directionality). c. Coarse-grained transition matrix from Fig. 2. Macrostates defined in this matrix were used to reorder cells in (b).
figures.attribution: Marius Lange; Volker Bergen; Michal Klein; Manu Setty; Bernhard Reuter; Mostafa Bakhti; et al.. CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping. DOI: 10.1038/s41592-021-01346-6. Source: NLM PMC OA Cloud. License: CC BY.

figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 5
figures.caption: Marker genes confirm CellRanks initial and terminal state annotations in the pancreas data.a. CellRank-computed initial and terminal states from Fig. 2d. b. Cells are colored based on the expression level of the indicated gene in each UMAP. The terminal states express the key marker genes relevant for each respective cell type. Showing for beta: Ins1 and Ins2 (insulin), alpha: Gcg (glucagon), epsilon: Ghrl (ghrelin), delta: Sst (somatostatin)33. For the initial state, we show expression of ductal cell markers Sox9, Anxa2 and Bicc124,33.
figures.attribution: Marius Lange; Volker Bergen; Michal Klein; Manu Setty; Bernhard Reuter; Mostafa Bakhti; et al.. CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping. DOI: 10.1038/s41592-021-01346-6. Source: NLM PMC OA Cloud. License: CC BY.

figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 6
figures.caption: CellRank recovers ductal and endocrine maturation.a. Published15 UMAP of the pancreas data24, colored by original cluster annotations, including all clusters in Fig. 2 as well as ductal cells. Streamlines show scVelo15 velocities. b. Cell cycle scores for S and G2M phase, computed using scanpy76 based on the gene set from ref. 107. Cycling cells mainly map to the ductal cluster. c. Spectrum of the CellRank-computed transition matrix. An eigengap appears after the first 5 eigenvalues, suggestive of 5 macrostates. d. UMAP showing 5 macrostates. e. Coarse-grained transition matrix. Diagonal elements give the stability index (SI) values. These automatically identify the Ductal 2, Epsilon, Alpha and Beta macrostates to be terminal. f. Fate probabilities towards the Ductal 2 state (‘ductal fate probability’). Among the 25 genes that correlate best with ductal fate probability in the ductal/Ngn3low clusters is Sox9, an established marker for ductal cell maturation33. g. Combined fate probabilities towards the Alpha, Beta and Epsilon macrostates (‘endocrine fate probability’). Among the 10 genes that correlate best with endocrine fate probability in the ductal/Ngn3low clusters are Ngn3 and Insm1, which are established endocrine progenitor markers33. Inset shows endocrine fate probabilities in the ductal/Ngn3low clusters. h. Ngn3 expression for the subset of cells shown in (g). Ngn3 expression correlates best with endocrine fate probabilities (Pearson correlation = 0.66).
figures.attribution: Marius Lange; Volker Bergen; Michal Klein; Manu Setty; Bernhard Reuter; Mostafa Bakhti; et al.. CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping. DOI: 10.1038/s41592-021-01346-6. Source: NLM PMC OA Cloud. License: CC BY.

figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 7
figures.caption: Splicing kinetics do not capture delta cell development.a. Phase portraits of the top 30 genes which are assigned the highest likelihoods by scVelo’s dynamical model of the mRNA lifecycle. Unspliced counts are on the x-axis, spliced counts are on the y-axis. Cells are colored according to the clusters from Fig. 2a. The solid purple curve is scVelo’s dynamical fit and the dashed purple line is scVelo’s inferred steady-state ratio. The top 30 genes are dominated by drivers for the alpha (Gcg33), epsilon (Ghrl33) and beta (Gng12108, Pdx134,70) lineages while delta drivers are not present. b. Phase portraits of known delta-associated genes Hhex35 and Cd24a38,39 as well as the CellRank-identified putative lineage driver Hadh. Cd24a was filtered out by scVelo’s gene filtering threshold because it only had unspliced counts in 3 cells (see box). Hhex could not be fit by scVelo because of too little expression and too large noise levels. Hadh could be fit by scVelo, however, delta cells are an outlier in this fit (see box) and were not correctly assigned to the steady-state. Thus, all three genes do not meaningfully contribute to velocity vectors towards delta cells.
figures.attribution: Marius Lange; Volker Bergen; Michal Klein; Manu Setty; Bernhard Reuter; Mostafa Bakhti; et al.. CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping. DOI: 10.1038/s41592-021-01346-6. Source: NLM PMC OA Cloud. License: CC BY.

figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 8
figures.caption: Projected velocities do not reveal how delta cells are generated.scVelo velocities projected onto the UMAP do not reveal a likely path towards delta cells. Velocities reveal short-range fate relationships but cannot be combined to give long-range fate predictions from looking at an embedding.

figures.caption: Cluster labels and timepoint annotations for lung data.a. Original cluster labels for the lung regeneration data52 in a UMAP projection. The data contains 24,882 murine lung epithelial cells sequenced using the Drop-seq workflow53 at 13 timepoints spanning days 2–15 past bleomycin injury. The ‘activated’ label refers to cell states that emerge after bleomycin injury. b. Same as (a) with timepoints colored in. Time points refer to time passed since bleomycin injury. c. figures.label: Extended Data Fig. 10
figures.caption: CellRank predicts a goblet to basal dedifferentiation trajectory.a. Cellrank identifies 9 macrostates. Airway cells, including club, goblet and basal cells, are highlighted. b. Single-cell fate probabilities of transitioning towards the basal state. A ‘band’ of cells within the goblet cluster exhibits high basal probability. c. Single-cell fate probabilities of transitioning towards the goblet state. Basal cells do not show any probability of transitioning towards the goblet state. d. Quantification of the results from (b) and (c). Goblet cells have a large probability of transitioning towards basal cells, but basal cells have no probability of transitioning towards the goblet state, confirming that the recovered trajectory proceeds from goblet to basal.

ai.title_zh: CellRank:面向单细胞命运图谱的有向推断方法
ai.summary_zh: 该资料介绍发表于 Nature Methods 的 CellRank 方法,其核心是将轨迹推断的稳健性与 RNA 速度提供的方向信息相结合,从而在方向未知的场景(如再生、重编程和疾病)中进行单细胞命运图谱构建。论文摘要与图注显示,该方法在胰腺发育数据上可自动识别初始、中间与终末群体,预测命运潜能并沿谱系展示连续基因表达趋势;在谱系示踪的细胞重编程数据中,预测的命运概率可恢复重编程结果;并预测了损伤后肺再生中的去分化轨迹及此前未知的中间细胞状态。提供的证据还包含若干基准分析 notebook 的静态观察记录,但作者代码未被执行,相关输入尺度与图号对应关系未明示。
learning_points: CellRank 将轨迹推断的稳健性与 RNA 速度的方向信息结合,用于方向未知的单细胞命运图谱构建(evidence: publication)。
方法建模考虑细胞命运决定的渐进性与随机性,以及速度向量中的不确定性(evidence: publication)。
Fig. 1 展示将 RNA 速度与细胞间相似性结合,以确定初始与终末状态并计算全局细胞命运潜能图谱(evidence: figure-0)。
Fig. 1 说明通过转录组差异向量与速度向量之间的相关性(即夹角 α)为邻域内细胞转移分配概率,并将有向转移矩阵粗粒化为四个宏观状态(evidence: figure-0)。
Fig. 2 展示在小鼠胰腺发育 E15.5 数据上使用 scVelo 投影速度并以流线呈现,CellRank 可给出早期细胞命运、终末状态识别及终末群体可能祖细胞等见解(evidence: figure-1)。
Fig. 3 展示对 Fev+ 激素阴性内分泌细胞进行正交子聚类,并用 CellRank 概率刻画获得终末 delta 命运的可能性及与 delta 命运概率相关的基因表达趋势(evidence: figure-2)。
Fig. 4 展示在 48,515 个 MEF 重编程为 iEP 的数据上,scVelo 速度未能揭示通向成功重编程的路径,而 CellRank 计算的宏观状态与命运概率可对应成功与死胡同状态(evidence: figure-3)。
提供的 notebook 静态观察显示存在 compute_time_benchmark 相关分析脚本,其中一处读取 morris_data 的 supp_table_4.csv 注释文件(evidence: script-2)。

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Overview of scXMatch. (a) Required inputs: N single-cell profiles xi, binary condition labels yi (orange/purple), a dissimilarity measure d, and the k parameter for k-NN mode. (b–c) A weighted graph G (complete or k-NN) is constructed, and a minimum-weight matching M is computed. (d) The number of cross-matches between conditions yields a P-value to assess global distribution shifts. (e–h) Examples using synthetic data sampled from bivariate normal distributions show that scXMatch detects significant shifts when distributions differ in mean (f, g) or variance (h), but not when they are identical (e).

(b–d) Peak memory usage (b), runtime (c), and relative coverage (d) as a function of k, for datasets with different numbers of samples N. Line plots and shaded areas in (b–d) depict means and 95% confidence intervals obtained for datasets with fixed N and k and varying dimensionality h∈{10,500,1000,2000}.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Benchmarking results on scRNA-seq data. (a) We used ten public scRNA-seq datasets from cells that were subject to perturbations of increasing strengths. (b) P-values obtained with the E-distance test (x-axes, results are identical for all four tested configurations) and scXMatch (y-axes) when comparing control against perturbed cell populations on the ten datasets (columns). Downwards arrows indicate alignment of P-values with perturbation strength. (c) Direct comparison of the relative coverages, required RAM, and runtimes of scXMatch and the E-distance test run in the default configuration suggested by the authors. (d–g) For comparison of our tool scXMatch against commonly used approaches that assess distribution shifts in scRNA-seq data we defined three metrics. (d) MI: Comparing cell populations with increasing perturbation strength against an unperturbed reference population should lead to increasing scores. (e) SSNR: Comparing a perturbed population against the reference should lead to a higher score than comparing disjoint subsets of the perturbed population against each other. (f) SR: Comparing different subsets of the reference against different subsets of the same perturbed condition should lead to similar scores as the comparison of the full data. (g) Benchmarking results of the nine approaches on all ten datasets. For eight of the datasets, scXMatch’s P-value is Pareto-optimal with regard to the three metrics (left panel).

figures.caption: Importance of dynamic imaging data for distinguishing RTM populations. (a) Snapshot of an unperturbed, sampling macrophage in vivo from the study by Schnitzerlein et al. (2025). Several morphological single-cell features (as schematically drawn on the image) were extracted. They characterize three categories of properties: static morphology, dynamic activity, or adaptation capabilities. ai.title_zh: scXMatch:量化单细胞数据中的分布偏移
ai.summary_zh: 该文献提出 scXMatch,一种基于非参数图检验的方法,用于量化任意具备合适距离度量的数据空间中的分布偏移。摘要称其在单细胞基因表达、染色质可及性和成像衍生细胞形态数据上进行了评估,并能稳健检测分布偏移。图 1 图注概述了方法流程:输入为 N 个单细胞谱、二值条件标签、相异度度量 d 以及 k-NN 模式的 k 参数,构建加权图(完全图或 k-NN 图)并计算最小权匹配,跨条件匹配数产生 P 值以评估全局分布偏移;合成双变量正态数据示例显示均值或方差不同时可检出显著偏移,分布相同时则不能。图 2 图注描述可扩展性测试,涉及 k-NN 图边数 |E| 与峰值内存、以及 k 与峰值内存、运行时间、相对覆盖率的关系。图 3 图注描述在十个公开 scRNA-seq 扰动数据集上的基准测试,并与 E-distance 检验比较 P 值、相对覆盖率、所需 RAM 和运行时间,同时定义 MI、SSNR、SR 三个指标。图 4 图注描述 Norman 数据集上 k∈{10,50,100} 时局部离群因子按是否纳入 MWMCM 着色,并标注 Wilcoxon 秩和检验 P 值。作者代码未运行,仅做静态检查,因此不构成复现验证。

方法基于非参数图检验,适用于任何具备合适距离度量的数据空间。
图 1 图注显示流程包括:输入单细胞谱、二值条件标签、相异度度量 d 与 k 参数,构建加权图(完全图或 k-NN 图),计算最小权匹配,并以跨条件匹配数得到 P 值。

图 3 图注显示在十个公开 scRNA-seq 扰动数据集上,将 scXMatch 与 E-distance 检验在 P 值、相对覆盖率、所需 RAM 和运行时间方面进行比较。

figures.label: Fig. 1.
figures.caption: DeCoRE retrieves accurate structural information using enhanced structural profile.(A) Schematic overview of DeCoRE for extracting structural information from nanopore sequencing data. In structure probing experiments, RNA was treated with structure probing chemicals (e.g., NAI-N3) or control reagent (DMSO) and sequenced using nanopore DRS. Then, DeCoRE aligned the reads together with their raw current signals to the reference RNA. For each nucleotide along the reference, a three-feature one-class SVM model was used to identify current signal anomalies in the chemical treated reads by comparing the matched bases, which were subsequently designated as modified bases. The resulting enhanced structural profile of the chemical-treated reads integrates both miscalled bases and modified bases. (B) Performance evaluation of structural profile incorporating both miscalled bases and modified bases in 150 mM Aclm-treated RNA. ROC curves analysis demonstrates strong agreement with known structural models of pri-miR-17∼92a RNA. Using only miscalled bases in Aclm-treated RNA yielded reasonably high agreement with the structural models. (C) ROC curves of reactivity scores calculated by DeCoRE and other methods (Materials and Methods), evaluated on known structural models of pri-miR-17∼92a RNA. (D) The six known structures of pri-miR-17∼92a RNA colored with the reactivity scores calculated by DeCoRE.

figures.label: Fig. 2.
figures.caption: DeCoRE identifies the known heterogenous structures of riboswitches.(A) Schematic of the clustering approach used to resolve heterogenous structures from enhanced structural profiles. Each read’s structural profile was encoded as a vector, where bases were categorized as 0 (matched bases, blue), 1 (modified bases, light blue), or 2 (miscalled bases, red). All vectors were padding to the same length (L) corresponding to the reference RNA. (B) Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) of the vectorized structural profile of each read in chemical-treated sample of the lysine riboswitch, colored by the cluster identified by DeCoRE. The silhouette score (si) was used to assess the clustering quality. The relative proportions of each cluster were indicated. (C) Barplots displayed the reactivity scores of the two structural cluster identified by DeCoRE in the region harboring the two mutually exclusive conformations of the lysine riboswitch—the antiterminator and transcription terminator states. The three key regions distinguishing the two conformations are highlighted by gray boxes and blue lines, and the base-pairing patterns in these regions for the two conformations was indicated by dashed lines. (D) The two structural models corresponding to the antiterminator and transcription terminator states were colored with the DeCoRE’s cluster-specific reactivity scores. (E) UMAP of the vectorized structural profile of each read in chemical-treated sample of the TPP riboswitch, colored by the cluster identified by DeCoRE. The relative proportions of each cluster were indicated. (F) The structure model of TPP riboswitch aptamer region (THI element) under ON and OFF state (24), colored with the DeCoRE’s cluster-specific reactivity scores. In the TPP-bound OFF state, J4/5 and J2/3 stack onto the TPP ligand, and loop L5 rearranges to form hydrogen bonds with P3, in contrast to the ON state.

figures.label: Fig. 3.
figures.caption: DeCoRE reveals structural transitions during B. subtilis 16S rRNA transcription.(A) Schematic overview of the experimental workflow used to generate the transcriptional intermediates of B. subtilis 16S rRNA in vitro and detect their structures using nanopore DRS–based structure probing method. (B) PCC of reactivity scores between each intermediate and the full-length 16S rRNA within their shared nucleotide regions. (C) Left heatmap showed the reactivity scores of 136 intermediates, categorized on the basis of their 3′ end alignment positions with 10-nt resolution. Each row represents the reactivity scores of a specific intermediate with length indicated by the y axis. Each column represents the reactivity score trajectories for a specific nucleotide, indicated along the x axis. Nucleotides highlighted with asterisk were examples [analyzed in (D)], which exhibit substantial reactivity score variation across different intermediates. Right line plot showed the read count distribution of each transcriptional intermediate. (D) Reactivity trajectories of three representative residues, corresponding to the highlighted nucleotides in (B), illustrate distinct structural transition patterns: G162 exhibits early base-pairing (“immediate pairing”), C192 remains unpaired across intermediates (“immediate unpaired”), and G178 shows mixed reactivity indicative of dynamic structural shifts. (E) Reactivity score profiles and predicted structure models of the selected intermediates of lengths 200 to 210 nt (L200_210), 300 to 310 nt (L300_310), and 600 to 610 nt (L600_610). The structure model of each intermediate was predicted using their all nucleotides with the reactivity scores as constraints.

ai.title_zh: DeCoRE:利用直接RNA测序解析RNA结构异质性的计算方法
ai.summary_zh: 该资料介绍了一种名为DeCoRE的计算方法,旨在利用直接RNA测序(DRS)数据解析单个转录本层面的RNA结构异质性与动态变化。摘要称DeCoRE结合增强的结构信号检测与测序读段直接聚类,可在单核苷酸分辨率下解析RNA结构集合,并以赖氨酸核糖开关、TPP核糖开关及细菌核糖体RNA共转录折叠路径作为展示案例。所提供的证据包含论文题录信息、四张图的图注以及若干脚本的静态观察记录,未包含作者代码运行结果或复现验证。
learning_points: DeCoRE被描述为面向直接RNA测序的结构探测数据计算方法,目标是在单个转录本层面解析RNA结构异质性与动态(证据:publication)。
图1图注描述了DeCoRE从纳米孔测序数据提取结构信息的流程:RNA经结构探测化学试剂(如NAI-N3)或对照试剂(DMSO)处理后进行纳米孔DRS测序,读段连同原始电流信号比对到参考RNA(证据:figure-0)。
图1图注提到对参考序列每个核苷酸使用三特征单类SVM模型,通过比较化学处理读段中的匹配碱基来识别电流信号异常,并将其指定为修饰碱基(证据:figure-0)。
图1图注说明增强的结构谱整合了误判碱基与修饰碱基,并在150 mM Aclm处理的RNA中评估其性能,ROC曲线分析显示与pri-miR-17∼92a RNA已知结构模型具有较强一致性(证据:figure-0)。
图2图注描述了从增强结构谱解析异质结构的聚类方法:每条读段的结构谱编码为向量,碱基分为0(匹配)、1(修饰)、2(误判)三类,并填充至参考RNA长度L(证据:figure-1)。
图2图注提到对赖氨酸核糖开关化学处理样本中各读段向量化结构谱进行UMAP降维,按DeCoRE识别的簇着色,并用轮廓系数评估聚类质量(证据:figure-1)。
图3图注描述了在体外生成枯草芽孢杆菌16S rRNA转录中间体并用基于纳米孔DRS的结构探测方法检测其结构的实验流程,以及136个中间体的反应性评分热图与读段计数分布(证据:figure-2)。
图4图注提到对五个高覆盖度16S rRNA转录中间体的化学处理样本读段向量化结构谱进行UMAP分析,并按DeCoRE识别的簇着色,同时展示PCA分析与50-nt滑窗PCC计算(证据:figure-3)。

figures.caption: Development of the MCCv platform.a, Schematic of the MCCv platform including: nanoscale chromatin structure, the regulatory landscape of the locus and phasing of other alleles in the locus. b, Schematic of the MCCv method. Oligonucleotide probes are designed over the variant of interest in heterozygous cells. Ultra-short-range ligation junctions (<800 bp) define the nanoscale topology at the variant. Long-range junctions (1 kb to 1 Mb) define the locus structure. c, Metaplots of MCCv nanoscale chromatin architecture heatmaps for inactive (reference) and active (alternate) alleles from 41 gain-of-function enhancer variants (Jurkat cells, six replicates, 1-bp bin size). The matrix represents the contact frequency between short-range ligation junctions (<800 bp) to visualize nanoscale chromatin architecture from single alleles. Below is a kernel density estimate (KDE) plot of genomic distances between two basepairs that make up the ultra-short-range ligation junctions for both reference and alternate alleles. d, Individual 2D nanoscale chromatin architecture heatmap for reference (left) and alternate (right) alleles of rs2793109 (1-bp bin size, n = 6, merged β = 0.75). The schematic is for nucleosome sliding with a fixed internucleosomal distance in the inactive alleles. At the nucleosome-depleted region, contacts between potential transcription factors in the alternate allele may lead to regions of high signal adjacent to transcription factor-binding sites. The underlying RUNX family motif is shown with the effect of the rs2793109 alternate allele highlighted. e, MCCv from rs2793109. A difference plot (reference minus alternate), DNase I sequencing and CTCF ChIP–seq are shown underneath. f, Using MCCv to phase other heterozygous variants within a locus. g, TT-seq skew from MCCv-phased variants in introns of ZNF438 (n = 13) and ZEB1 (n = 15) (mean ± s.e.m., Wilcoxon’s signed-rank test, paired, two-sided, two-stage step-up procedure for multiple-test correction: ZNF438 q = 0.435; ZEB1 q = 0.0002). figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.caption: Direct read-out of genome editing with MCCv.a, Schematic illustrating coupling of basepair-level editing technologies with basepair resolution MCCv. Incomplete genome editing is leveraged to make a population of cells with mixed alleles become deconvoluted with the platform’s single-allele capabilities. b, Base editing experimental design with CTCF guide RNA sequence as well as locations of rs4409785 and the CTCF motif shown. The location of an upstream control guide outside the extended CTCF motif but within the MCC capture oligonucleotide is also shown. c, Experimental set-up of the CTCF and control edits in primary T cells. Edits were performed in parallel and mixed to avoid double editing. The cell mix was then fixed and captured by MCCv. As these cells were heterozygous for risk variant rs4409785 this led to six different editing outcomes that were deconvoluted by single-allele MCCv. To increase the depth of the data, six independent replicates were performed. d, Allele-specific (relative to rs4409785) editing efficiency of BE4max in primary CD4+ T cell for both control and CTCF guides. Editing efficiencies are shown as a percentage of NGS reads with C-to-T substitution. Where multiple Cs could be edited, the one with highest editing efficiency is shown (n = 2 independent experiments, mean ± s.d.). e, Edit-MCCv tracks for reference (purple) and alternate (green) alleles of rs4409785 with wild-type, control edit and CTCF edit shown. figures.caption: Further characterisation of MCC derived regulatory contacts at GWAS loci.a, Quantification of normalized MCC junctions at the genes in the multi-trait locus for all variants shown in Fig. 2c (n = 18 (3 donors, with 6 independent MCC libraries each), mean ± s.d., paired Student’s t-test, two-sided, two-stage step-up method for multiple test correction, P values reported in source data). b, Enrichment of variant–promoter ligation junctions compared to background between Micro-C (median = 1.33) and MCC (median = 5.5). ai.title_zh: 调控变异的单等位基因纳米尺度定位
ai.summary_zh: 该资料为 Nature Genetics 期刊论文《Single-allele nanoscale mapping of regulatory variants》(DOI:10.1038/s41588-026-02776-8)的题录与图注信息。摘要称作者开发了基于单等位基因染色质结构分析的 Micro Capture-C 变异到功能平台(MCCv),可在纳米尺度识别染色质结构变化、将顺式调控元件中的变异与靶基因关联、对位点内其他杂合变异进行定相,并在基因组编辑后直接读取变异对染色质互作的影响;摘要还称在 CD4+ T 细胞中研究了 405 个与免疫介导炎症性疾病相关的顺式调控元件,发现一种通过产生新 CTCF 基序阻断超级增强子与 SESN3 启动子接触的功能获得机制。图注显示 Fig.1 介绍 MCCv 平台与纳米尺度热图,Fig.2 展示用 MCC 将 GWAS 变异关联到基因,Fig.3 展示 MCCv 识别改变染色质结构的 GWAS 变异,Fig.4 展示 rs4409785 通过功能获得性 CTCF 位点发挥作用。所附代码证据仅为若干脚本的静态读取观察,未运行。
learning_points: MCCv 平台的设计思路:针对杂合细胞中感兴趣的变异设计寡核苷酸探针,用超短程连接接头(<800 bp)定义变异处的纳米尺度拓扑,用长程接头(1 kb 至 1 Mb)定义位点结构(evidence: figure-0)。
单等位基因可视化方式:Fig.1c 以 1 bp 分箱的接触频率矩阵展示参考等位与替代等位的纳米尺度染色质结构,并配核密度估计(KDE)图展示超短程连接接头的基因组距离分布(evidence: figure-0)。
将 GWAS 变异关联到基因:Fig.2 结合外周血 scATAC-seq 的 UMAP、单倍型机制分配热图、CD4+ T 细胞的 Micro-C/ATAC-seq/CTCF ChIP-seq 轨迹,展示变异-启动子接触(evidence: figure-1)。
方法灵敏度对比:Fig.2d 比较 MCC 与 Micro-C 识别到的变异-启动子连接接头数量,MCC 中位数为 828.2,Micro-C 中位数为 2.07(n = 349 个启动子接触,两种方法各 2 个独立文库)(evidence: figure-1)。
变异效应的统计评估:Fig.3a 对杂合 SNP 的 MCCv 峰计算替代/参考归一化连接计数,采用配对双侧 Student t 检验与局部 FDR 估计;Fig.3c 用双侧 χ2 检验比较显著 MCCv 变化变异比例并给出对照富集(evidence: figure-2)。
调控元件类别与变异效应:Fig.3b 以聚类层次热图展示不同调控元件类别上替代/参考连接计数平均比值(evidence: figure-2)。
功能获得性 CTCF 位点案例:Fig.4 围绕 rs4409785 展示 GWAS 关联火山图、CTCF 共识基序与序列比对、1 bp 分辨率的 MCCv 足迹与纳米尺度热图,以及杂合供体中 CTCF ChIP-seq、ATAC-seq、H3K27ac ChIP-seq 的等位偏斜(evidence: figure-3)。

ai.title_zh: 简化大型底栖无脊椎动物生物多样性评估:面向高碎屑量样本的标准化宏条形码方法
ai.summary_zh: 该文献提出并测试了一种标准化方法,用于处理未将大型底栖无脊椎动物从网采物中分离的踢网/扫网合并样本,通过DNA宏条形码估算物种多样性。样本采自大墨尔本地区10个土地利用、无脊椎动物丰度与多样性以及采样碎屑类型和体积各异的站点。方法包含筛分、混合和DNA提取流程,以减少大块碎屑、石块和沙,并富集无脊椎动物用于宏条形码。研究使用各站点样本干重的不同百分比作为DNA来源,发现处理20%至40%干重时回收的物种多样性大体一致,但对总干重低的样本建议设定最低干重。文中给出了实验室与生物信息学工作流程,并配有展示样本处理流程、ASV与序列读长分类归属、物种与科检出总数以及不同干重百分比下物种检出平均比例的图。
learning_points: 论文提出一种针对未分离无脊椎动物的高碎屑量样本的标准化DNA宏条形码处理流程。

流程包括筛分、混合和DNA提取,用于减少大块碎屑、石块和沙并富集无脊椎动物。
研究以样本干重的不同百分比作为DNA来源,比较不同比例下回收的物种多样性。
结果显示处理20%至40%干重时回收的物种多样性大体一致,但对总干重低的样本建议设定最低干重。

figures.label: FIGURE 1
figures.caption: Study sites and experimental design for the 2018 dataset. The survey covered 12 sites distributed across three regions of the north‐western Mediterranean coast (France). Each site hosted three Autonomous Reef Monitoring Structures (ARMS), and each ARMS comprised nine plates providing 17 colonizable faces. (a) Map of the 12 study sites grouped by region. (b) Photography‐based analysis: Images of the 17 faces from a single ARMS, arranged in five columns representing the main structural face categories (9T, BO = bottom open, TO = top open, BC = bottom closed, TC = top closed). Bottom right, an example of random points overlaid on a photograph for taxonomic labelling by an expert assisted by artificial intelligence. (c–d) Metabarcoding design for one of the 10 sites where one ARMS was analysed face by face. (c) 17 separate sessile samples corresponding to the 17 faces, allowing direct comparison with the photographic data. (d) Pooled sessile fractions from each of the other two ARMS at the same site, processed as a single metabarcoding sample following the standard NOAA protocol. Only the 10 sites (out of 12) that followed the design illustrated in this figure and in Table 1 were used for comparative purposes.

figures.label: FIGURE 2
figures.caption: Taxa rarefaction and extrapolation curves. The number of metabarcoding molecular operational taxonomic units (mOTUs) or photographic taxonomic labels is plotted on the vertical axis as a function of the number of photographic or metabarcoding samples on the horizontal axis. Curves represent three types of Hill numbers defined by the q parameter: Taxonomic richness (q = 0), i.e., the number of labels or mOTUs (black); Shannon‐like diversity (q = 1), i.e., the exponential of Shannon entropy (grey); and Simpson‐like diversity (q = 2), i.e., the inverse of Simpson concentration (light grey). Shaded areas denote standard‐error confidence intervals. The metabarcoding dataset here corresponds to the 17‐faces design (for comparisons with photography).

ai.title_zh: ARMS 宏条形码中分面处理提升海洋生物多样性监测:跨方案、实验设计与影像调查的比较
ai.summary_zh: 该研究将影像分析与 COI 宏条形码结合,在西北地中海 10 个站点比较并优化基于 ARMS 的监测方案:先优化实验室流程(DNA 提取与聚合酶选择),并采用受控、考虑重复的 VTAM 流程以减少假阳性;随后首次对影像与 eDNA 的 α、β 多样性进行逐面(face-by-face)比较,即对每个 ARMS 面单独做宏条形码而非混合样本。摘要称宏条形码检出约 15 倍更高的站点水平丰富度,并与地理距离和环境梯度呈更强相关;逐面处理比 NOAA 混合方案获得更高丰富度和更强的 β 多样性—距离相关;将 17 个面归为五个结构类别可作为更可操作的替代方案。图注显示 2018 数据集覆盖 12 个站点、每站 3 个 ARMS、每个 ARMS 9 块板共 17 个可定殖面,其中 10 个站点按逐面设计分析。
learning_points: 研究将影像分析与 COI 宏条形码结合,用于比较和优化基于 ARMS 的海洋生物多样性监测方案(evidence: publication)。
实验设计层面:2018 数据集覆盖西北地中海 12 个站点,每站 3 个 ARMS,每个 ARMS 由 9 块板提供 17 个可定殖面(evidence: figure-0)。
影像分析将 17 个面按五个主要结构类别排列(9T、BO 底部开放、TO 顶部开放、BC 底部封闭、TC 顶部封闭),并在照片上叠加随机点供专家借助人工智能进行类群标注(evidence: figure-0)。
宏条形码设计对比两种方式:对同一站点一个 ARMS 的 17 个面分别取样逐面分析,与对同站另外两个 ARMS 的固着组分按 NOAA 标准方案混合为单一样本(evidence: figure-0)。
图注说明仅 12 个站点中的 10 个遵循该逐面与混合对比设计(evidence: figure-0)。
稀释与外推曲线以 mOTU 数或影像类群标签数为纵轴、样本数为横轴,展示 q=0 丰富度、q=1 Shannon 类多样性与 q=2 Simpson 类多样性,阴影为标准的误差置信区间(evidence: figure-1)。
门水平组成条形图按方法与板面展示相对丰富度与相对丰度;脊索动物主要为海鞘而非鱼类,鱼类在影像数据中缺失且在宏条形码中相对稀少;未归类 mOTU 未显示,稀疏类群合并为深灰类别(evidence: figure-2)。
方案对比图按站点展示逐面合并(17 个面样本合计)与 NOAA 混合(两个整 ARMS 固着组分样本合计)的丰富度与门水平相对丰度,并提示两面板纵轴尺度不同(evidence: figure-3)。

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Graphical abstract of the spatio-temporal study of arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis between rice and Rhizophagus irregularis. a) Simplified representation of the biological system of study, the mutualism between roots of rice (Oryza sativa) and the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus (AMF) R. irregularis, with the macroscopic view of the interaction on the left, and the microscopic view of symbiotic fungal structures outside and within the plant root on the right. b) Schematic representation of the high-resolution experimental techniques employed in this study to resolve the spatio-temporal dynamics of AM symbiosis. On the left, Molecular Cartography by Resolve Biosciences, including a simplified mycorrhizal root section with 4 genes detected. FISH, fluorescence in situ hybridization. On the right, Translating-Ribosome Affinity Purification (TRAP) RNA sequencing using AM-stage specific promoters, indicating the structure of the TRAP construct (with a 6x-His-FLAG as well as GFP tags fused to the ribosomal protein RLP18) and hypothetical expression pattern of the construct based on AM-stage specific promoter used.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Molecular cartography of R. irregularis-colonized rice roots reveals substantial transcriptional repatterning at quantitative and spatial levels. a) Heatmap of log2 fold-changes (log2FC) for comparisons of transcript spot data between inoculation regimes and root types. Significance levels as determined by DESeq2 shown with asterisks (* for P-value <0.05, ** for <0.01, *** for <0.001). Gene names are colored based on species (blue for R. irregularis, black for rice). Dots next to rice genes indicate those with previous knowledge regarding their expression pattern (for gene specifically expressed in arbusculated cells, cyan if known for rice, magenta if only known in other species) or involvement in AM symbiosis (green if known function in rice or other species). CR, crown root; LLR, large lateral root; Ri, Rhizophagus irregularis inoculation. b) Composite image of DAPI (magenta) and WGA-AF488 (cyan) of an R. irregularis-inoculated (+Ri) large lateral root (LLR) section for visualization of nuclei, cell boundaries and fungal structures. The composite is placed on a black background, and image is reused in Figs. 2c, 2d, 3a, 3d, 4b, 4e, Figure S6, S7. Close-up A1 showcases all fungal structures visualized: intraradical hyphae (IH), arbuscules at distinct development stages (developing, dA; mature, mA; and collapsing, cA), and vesicles (V). Close-up A2 showcases the difference between plant (red), and fungal (white arrow) nuclei. c) Image-transcript overlays showing spatial expression of cell-type specific markers in a −Ri and a +Ri section, both of large lateral roots. −Ri image is reused in Figures S2a, S4, S7. d) Image-transcript overlays highlighting spatial patterning of OsSWEET12 in a −Ri and a +Ri section, both of large lateral roots. DAPI/WGA-AF488 composite in white, placed on a black background, different colors correspond to independent transcripts, each spot corresponds to 1 detected transcript. Dotted square and arrows highlight transcript abundance heterogeneity between arbuscules at the same developmental stage. Scale bar, 100 μm.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Molecular cartography highlights heterogeneity in fungal and plant transcript abundances across mycorrhizal structures at the same or distinct developmental stages. a) Image-transcript overlays comparing spatial expression of plant and fungal transcripts in an inoculated (+Ri) large lateral root (LLR) section: (i) plant AM marker genes, (ii) fungal genes, (iii) 1 plant AM marker and 1 fungal gene. DAPI/WGA-AF488 composite in white, different colors correspond to independent transcripts, each spot corresponds to 1 detected transcript. Dotted square and arrows highlight transcript abundance heterogeneity between arbuscules at the same developmental stage. b) Quantification of transcript abundance in distinct R. irregularis colonization structures in Molecular Cartography +Ri sections. Vesicles and arbusculated-cells from several sections were manually segmented in ImageJ and transcript spot counts for all transcripts in each individual structure quantified. Each graph corresponds to 1 transcript, name above. Each spot corresponds to the transcript per μm2 value for an individual structure (arbuscule or vesicle), n = 96 for arbuscules, n = 67 for vesicles. P-value of T-student test between structures indicated in each graph. c) Association between fungal nuclei and transcripts in vesicles of in an inoculated (+Ri) crown root (CR) section. Left panels show composite image of DAPI (magenta) and WGA-AF488 (cyan) for visualization of nuclei, cell boundaries and fungal structures. Right panel shows image-transcript overlays for fungal genes; DAPI/WGA-AF488 composite in white, different colors correspond to independent transcripts, each spot corresponds to 1 detected transcript. Image is reused in Figures S2b, S3, S6, S7 and S8. First row for full section, second row for magnified vesicles, location indicated on first row. d) Image-transcript overlays showing spatial expression of the 7 most abundant plant phosphate transporters in an inoculated (+Ri) large lateral root (LLR) section. Close-ups D1 to D3 highlight differing spatial detection patterns in diverse cell types: D1 in emerging lateral root, D2 and D3 for arbuscules at distinct developmental stages and non-colonized cortical cells. Arrows highlight clusters of OsPT4, OsPT8 and OsPT13 transcripts around plant nuclei of non-colonized and collapsing arbuscule-containing cells. DAPI/WGA-AF488 composite in white, different colors correspond to independent transcripts, each spot corresponds to 1 detected transcript. Scale bar, 100 μm. e) Image-transcript overlays demonstrating transcript abundance heterogeneity of mature arbuscules. Arbuscules extracted from various inoculated (+Ri) crown and large lateral root sections. Left panels show composite image of DAPI (magenta) and WGA-AF488 (cyan) for visualization of nuclei, cell boundaries and fungal structures. Right panel shows image-transcript overlays for fungal genes; DAPI/WGA-AF488 composite in white, different colors correspond to independent transcripts, each spot corresponds to 1 detected transcript. All composite images are placed on a black background.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: Co-localization and cell segmentation analyses for molecular cartography mycorrhizal samples reveal distinct clusters of co-localized transcripts and cell populations. a) Colocalization heatmap of transcript colocalization scores for +Ri sections. Colocalization scores between each gene pair, quantifying the frequency of finding transcripts in spatial proximity at pixel resolution, were determined using the Polylux plugin (Resolve Biosciences) in ImageJ. Note that the colocalization matrix is asymmetric (x-axis represents the starting transcript searching its neighborhood; y-axis represents transcripts found in that search). Genes with >0.2 self-co-localisation scores were used for analysis and subjected to hierarchical clustering. Distinct clusters are indicated by thicker boundaries between genes. Color scale represents the transcript colocalization (CL) score. b) Image-transcript overlays highlighting the spatial expression of key marker genes in selected colocalization clusters in an inoculated (+Ri) large lateral root (LLR) section. DAPI/WGA-AF488 composite in white, placed on a black background, different colors correspond to independent transcripts, each spot corresponds to 1 detected transcript. Dotted square and arrows highlight transcript abundance heterogeneity between arbuscules at the same developmental stage. Scale bar, 100 μm. c) UMAP projection of segmented cells, color indicates the cluster (A to F) assigned to each cell by Seurat single-cell analysis, number of cells in each cluster indicated in the legend. d) Heatmap of normalized scaled transcript counts for each cell (columns) for the top 10 marker genes (rows) in each cell cluster (column sections), and their relative expression level compared with other clusters. e) Assignment of clusters to segmented cells based on Seurat single-cell analyses in an inoculated (+Ri) large lateral root (LLR) section. DAPI/WGA-AF488 composite in white, placed on a black background, segmented cells in colored lines, distinct colors for separate clusters (“Unassigned cluster” used for cells filtered out during quality control in single-cell analysis). Dotted square (magnified below) and arrows highlight transcript abundance heterogeneity between arbuscules at the same developmental stage. Scale bar, 100 μm.

ai.title_zh: 细胞分辨率下丛枝菌根共生时空调控研究
ai.summary_zh: 该论文研究水稻(Oryza sativa)根系被不规则根瘤菌(Rhizophagus irregularis)定殖后丛枝菌根(AM)共生的时空调控。摘要称研究采用单细胞分辨率空间转录组学分析植物与真菌基因,发现真菌结构间转录活性差异及植物细胞身份标记的重编程,并观察到发育阶段相似的丛枝细胞存在显著转录异质性;同时使用AM阶段特异性启动子的TRAP-seq进行翻译阶段解析分析,发现核糖体结合转录本群体的广泛时空变化,以及细胞壁合成基因和防御标记在丛枝寿命早期低丰度、晚期高丰度的模式。图注显示Figure 1为图形摘要,Figure 2为分子制图热图与显微图像,Figure 3为转录本丰度异质性分析,Figure 4为共定位与细胞分割分析。作者代码未运行,仅作静态观察,未验证复现结果。
learning_points: 论文摘要提出以单细胞分辨率空间转录组学同时检测植物与真菌基因,用于解析AM共生建立过程。
摘要指出定殖后植物细胞身份标记发生重编程,且发育阶段相似的丛枝细胞之间存在显著转录异质性。
摘要描述使用AM阶段特异性启动子的TRAP-seq进行翻译阶段解析分析,观察到核糖体结合转录本群体的时空变化。
摘要提到细胞壁生物合成基因与防御标记在丛枝早期低丰度、晚期高丰度,提示宿主驱动的丛枝终止转变。
Figure 1图注展示研究系统的宏观与微观示意,以及Molecular Cartography与TRAP-seq两种高分辨率实验技术的示意。
Figure 2图注展示接种处理与根类型比较的log2FC热图,并标注DESeq2显著性水平与基因物种来源颜色。

figures.label: Fig 1
figures.caption: Workflow of the computational design.Muscle tissue was extracted from the injured and non-injured hindlimb of young and geriatric mice at 3 and 7 days post-injury. Basal cells were extracted from the non-injured limb, and senescent and non-senescent cells were taken from the injured limb. Three cell types of interest were isolated by FACS using well-established markers for myeloid cells, FAPs, and satellite cells. Senescent cells were further sorted using SPiDER-β-gal, as previously described [20]. Low input RNA-seq was performed for all three cell states: basal, senescent, and non-senescent, leading to initial gene expression matrix consisting of 108 samples each, with 46078 genes. This matrix was serially filtered to remove dropouts and non-discriminant genes. The final 142×36 matrix was then used to build two networks, one of genes and the other of conditions. Feature selection was then performed by combining eigenvector centrality of the gene network with community selection of the condition network. The process culminates in the identification of a small number of senescence-associated genes. Created in BioRender. Garcia-Ojalvo, J. (2026) https://BioRender.com/n1qw8gc.

figures.caption: Dropout filtering.(A) The initial expression matrix consisted of 108 samples each defined by 46 078 genes. The 108 samples arise from 36 different cell conditions, each with 3 replicates. The first filtering consisted of averaging the expression of each gene among the 3 replicates of each condition and removing the ones whose expression was equal to 0 in at least 2 out of 3 replicates (gene cases A and C). This combination of averaging and filtering led to an expression matrix of 36 samples (representing the different cell conditions) and 28 603 genes. (B) Principal component analysis of the remaining data, with cell conditions sorted either by cell type (left) or cell state (right).

figures.caption: Significance filtering.(A) We compared the gene-expression distributions of the conditions between the senescent cell state and the non-senescent and basal states grouped together, for each one of the 28 603 genes. The distributions were compared by using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and applying a Bonferroni correction to the p-value of 0.05. A total of 142 genes passed the test. (B) Principal component analysis of the remaining data, with cell conditions sorted either by cell type (left) or cell state (right).

(B) Principal component analysis of the remaining data, with cell conditions sorted either by cell type (left) or cell state (right).

figures.label: Fig 5
figures.caption: Network-community assessment.(A) Once the ECFS ranking was obtained we constructed cell-state networks, as described in the main text. (B) ECFS ranking performance for increasing number of genes, when comparing the non-senescent phenotype with the rest. The h score and the number of communities are plotted in the top and bottom panels, respectively. The best h-score of 0.737 was obtained when considering the first 10 genes. The vertical and horizontal red dashed lines correspond to the optimal h score and the three communities, respectively. (C,D) For that case we obtain the best community separation, represented here. The genes listed on panel C give rise to 3 communities, each one predominantly consisting of a single cell state –basal, senescent or non-senescent– (shown in blue, orange, and green, respectively). The node labels have the format AnB, where A is either Y or G, corresponding to the sample coming from a young or geriatric mouse, respectively, n is either 3 or 7, corresponding to day 3 or day 7 after the injury, and B is either M, F or S, corresponding to the myeloid, FAP or satellite cell type, respectively.

figures.caption: Transcription factors regulating the identified genes and their role in senescence.The transcription factors from the most relevant protein-coding genes identified by our approach are grouped by color, representing the pathways they are involved in, as established by their Gene Ontology (GO) annotations. We use MyGene.info to query the GO database (https://mygene.info). Information about transcriptional interactions is obtained from SCENIC [62]. The python script to query the GO database and identify the transcription factor categories can be found in the paper’s public software repository, https://github.com/dsb-lab/CellularSenescence.

License: CC BY.

figures.label: Fig 10
figures.caption: Entropy calculation.To obtain the total entropy Htot, first, we have to calculate the individual entropies, both cell type-wise and community-wise. Since a total of 12 senescent, 12 non-senescent and 12 basal cells were present in our analysis, in the cell type-wise entropy computation, the probability pi is defined as the probability of a cell found in a community to belong to a given cell state. In the community-wise entropy calculation, the probability pi is defined by the ratio of cells belonging to a specific cell state to the overall number of cells within that community. The total entropy Htot is calculated by summing all the individual cell type-wise and community-wise entropies. The normalized entropy value h is obtained by normalizing the total entropy Htot with the maximum possible entropy Hmax that corresponds to the case when each cell belongs to its own separate community.

figures.label: Fig 11
figures.caption: Histogram of randomly computed h-scores.The h-scores represented in the histogram were computed by permuting the cell conditions labels. The artificially created labels were sorted into 2 classes, one consisting of non-senescent cells and the other of senescent and basal cells. The ECFS algorithm was performed for the classes, and the corresponding networks with the communities were computed. The h-score obtained for the 10 best-performing genes was extracted. The described procedure was repeated 1000 times and the corresponding h-scores are shown in the histogram. The red line represents the original maximum h-score obtained by our separation (h = 0.737). The p-value for our obtained h-score to be part of this distribution was found to be 0.00019.

figures.label: Figure 1.
figures.caption: Schematic of the workflow of the study.We analyzed genome-wide methylation and genotyping data from blood samples from 621 AD and non-demented control individuals from the MAGENTA study. To replicate our findings, we analyzed data from 1394 healthy African Americans from the GENOA study, 422 healthy African Americans from the Grady Trauma Project, and 729 healthy Whites from the NSPHS study. We applied a set of first-, second-, and third-generation methylation clocks to the individuals and estimated their genetic ancestry. This enabled us to explore the performance of methylation clocks in individuals with different genetic ancestries.

Importantly, coloring the samples by cohort, sample center, sex, disease status, ethnicity, and sample plate did not show any outright stratification across the two PCs.

The correlation of r=0.72\begin{document}$r=0.72$\end{document} is consistent with previous studies of similar age groups. (B) Pearson correlation between chronological age and DNAm age predicted by the Horvath clock for the genetically admixed cohorts in MAGENTA. The cohorts with substantial African ancestry—African Americans and Puerto Ricans—exhibit lower correlations (r=0.51\begin{document}$r=0.51$\end{document} and 0.45, respectively) compared to the Cubans (r=0.68\begin{document}$r=0.68$\end{document}) and Peruvians (r=0.72\begin{document}$r=0.72$\end{document}). (C) Relative accuracy of the Horvath clock across cohorts compared to Whites. The bar plot shows the difference in Pearson correlation coefficients relative to the White cohort baseline (r=0.72\begin{document}$r=0.72$\end{document}). Asterisks indicate a statistically significant difference from the baseline (* p < 0.05). Error bars denote 95% confidence intervals for relative correlation differences (Zou's method).

Cohorts with substantial African ancestry (African American and Puerto Rican, red bars) consistently exhibit lower correlations compared to Whites, Peruvians, and Cubans across all three clock models. Asterisks indicate a statistically significant difference in correlation compared to the White MAGENTA cohort baseline (* p < 0.05).

figures.caption: Methylation clocks do not consistently identify accelerated aging in admixed Alzheimer’s cohorts.(A) Comparison of the distributions of Horvath intrinsic age acceleration for AD patients and non-demented controls for each of the admixed cohorts in MAGENTA. AD patients do not show significantly higher age acceleration in any of the admixed cohorts. In contrast, the AD cases had significantly greater acceleration than controls in the white cohort (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). NS, not significant. (B) Median differences (in years) in intrinsic age acceleration between AD patients and non-demented controls for five methylation clocks for each cohort in MAGENTA. (C) The allele frequency distribution of the single nucleotide variants that disrupt CpG sites considered by the Horvath clock in 76,156 individuals from gnomAD (v3.0). ai.title_zh: DNA甲基化时钟在遗传混合个体中泛化能力不足
ai.summary_zh: 该研究基于MAGENTA研究中621名阿尔茨海默病(AD)患者与匹配对照(非裔美国人、西班牙裔、白人队列)的血液全基因组甲基化与基因分型数据,评估第一、二、三代甲基化时钟的表现,并在GENOA(1394名健康非裔美国人)、Grady Trauma Project(422名健康非裔美国人)和NSPHS(729名健康白人)三个额外数据集中进行重复分析。结果显示,与白人队列相比,甲基化时钟在遗传混合队列中预测年龄的准确性更低,尤其在非洲祖源比例较高的个体中;这一准确性下降在额外数据集中同样存在。时钟也未能一致地识别混合AD病例相对于对照的年龄加速。通过将时钟CpG与全球人群的甲基化、胚系遗传变异及甲基化QTL(meQTL)数据取交集,研究发现非洲与欧洲祖源个体间时钟CpG的差异甲基化较为常见,遗传变异很少破坏人群间的时钟CpG,但相当一部分时钟CpG的meQTL在非洲遗传祖源中频率显著更高。
learning_points: 研究使用MAGENTA队列621名AD患者与匹配对照的血液全基因组甲基化与基因分型数据,并估计遗传祖源(Figure 1)。
研究在GENOA(1394名健康非裔美国人)、Grady Trauma Project(422名健康非裔美国人)和NSPHS(729名健康白人)三个额外数据集中重复分析(Figure 1)。
Horvath时钟在白人MAGENTA队列中年龄与DNAm年龄的Pearson相关为r=0.72,而在非裔美国人和波多黎各人队列中分别为r=0.51和0.45,低于古巴人(r=0.68)和秘鲁人(r=0.72)(Figure 2)。
MAGENTA各队列的年龄分布差异不能解释队列间时钟准确性的显著差异(Figure 1—figure supplement 1)。
MAGENTA甲基化数据的PCA中,PC1解释14.96%、PC2解释8.63%的方差,按队列、样本中心、性别、疾病状态、族裔和样本板着色未显示明显分层(Figure 1—figure supplement 2)。
研究将时钟CpG与甲基化、胚系遗传变异和meQTL数据取交集,发现非洲与欧洲祖源个体间时钟CpG差异甲基化常见,遗传变异很少破坏人群间时钟CpG,但相当一部分时钟CpG的meQTL在非洲遗传祖源中频率显著更高。
静态检查显示脚本scripts/07_meqtl_overlap_analysis.R读取ancestry_CpGs.RData、all_meqtl_affected_cpgs.rds、all_results.rds和clock_cpgs_overlap_tidy.csv等文件(script-0)。
静态检查显示脚本scripts/11_assemble_figures.R使用ggsave输出Figure2.pdf、Figure3.pdf和Figure6.pdf(script-1)。

ai.title_zh: 去卵巢小鼠下丘脑进行性神经炎症与女性人下丘脑衰老相关转录组变化相平行
ai.summary_zh: 该研究对去卵巢(OVX)后小鼠下丘脑进行时间序列表征,结合生理测量与后部下丘脑(PH)和视前区(POA)的 bulk RNA-seq,时间点为 OVX 后 14 天和 4 个月。摘要称血清促黄体生成素水平先进行性升高后下降,核心体温早期达峰后恢复正常;转录组分析显示炎症通路、胶质标志物和 KNDy 神经元相关基因网络呈时间依赖性激活,4 个月时变化最明显,尤其在 PH。免疫荧光显示雌激素长期撤除后弓状核内神经激肽 B 释放增加、KNDy 神经元活动下降、星形胶质细胞反应性增强。研究还分析公开的人下丘脑 RNA-seq 数据,发现年龄相关转录组模式(包括进行性炎症信号、胶质激活和 KNDy 基因表达改变)与 OVX 小鼠模型显著相关,尤其在通路水平。
learning_points: 图 1 展示了 OVX 后小鼠下丘脑的生理与转录组变化设计:包括实验设计示意、血清 LH 在 7、14、21 天及 1、2、4 个月的测量、核心体温测量,以及 PH 和 POA 的 Hallmark 基因集归一化富集分数热图。
图 2 以火山图展示 OVX 后差异表达基因:PH 14 天 vs 完整组 13 个蛋白编码 DEG,PH 4 个月 vs 完整组 82 个,POA 14 天 vs 完整组 14 个,POA 4 个月 vs 完整组 70 个,阈值为 FDR < 0.05。

figures.label: FIGURE 1
figures.caption: Design of AOE‐Net and PAAG for aging acceleration and chronic disease risk prediction. (a) Diagram of the whole workflow, including pre‐training and fine‐tuning of AOE‐Net, and the computation of PAAG. PAAG quantifies the age gap relative to a population‐based reference which is different to conventional AG. (b) Detailed architecture of AOE‐Net and the computational pipeline for PAAG. Of note, the Product of Experts (PoE) approach is used to derive the joint latent representation from multi‐omics inputs, thus AOE‐Net can effectively leverage both unpaired and paired data during pre‐training and fine‐tuning stages. Especially in this work, AOE‐Net is pre‐trained on normal samples, encompassing unpaired RNA‐seq and DNA methylation profiles from the GTEx dataset, alongside paired RNA‐seq and DNA methylation data from TCGA normal samples, guided by personalized‐context‐aware enhanced contrastive learning. The model then can be fine‐tuned to predict biological age and compute PAAG. (c) Downstream applications of PAAG in diverse biological and clinical contexts. PAAG is utilized to predict or correlate with different phenotypes, including survival outcome, disease severity, immune response and omics‐based biomarker relevant to both aging and disease.

figures.label: FIGURE 2
figures.caption: Identifying overall survival and immune response stratification in pan‐cancer populations by AOE‐Net and PAAG. (a) Diagram illustrating the relationship between chronological age and predicted biological age by AOE‐Net, with PAAG quantifying the deviation for population reference. (b) Kaplan–Meier survival curves stratified by PAAG‐defined aging groups (decelerated, normal, and accelerated) across pan‐cancer patients, analyzed within young (< 40 years), middle‐aged (40–60 years), and old (> 60 years) chronological age subgroups. The aging‐accelerated individuals consistently show the poorest overall survival. p‐values for each subgroup are shown (log‐rank test). (c) Hazard Ratios (HR) for overall survival prediction using various omics aging clocks (e.g., DeepMAge, BiT age clock, PhenoAge and horvathAge) compared to AOE‐Net‐derived PAAG along with ablation experiment. Results are presented for young, middle, and old age subgroups. (d) Concordance Index (C‐index) for overall survival prediction using different omics aging clocks (DeepMAge, BiT age clock, PhenoAge and horvathAge) compared to AOE‐Net‐derived PAAG. Results are presented for young, middle, and old age subgroups. PAAG consistently shows superior predictive accuracy, especially in the young and middle age subgroups. (e) Hazard ratios (HR) comparison for pan‐cancer overall survival analysis using different age regression methods combined with new PAAG or conventional AG, in a manner of ablation study too. (f) The differential distributions of biological age (PAAG) and chronological age across tumor immune subtypes. (g) The variation of ICS5 scores across PAAG‐defined aging groups (Kruskal‐Wallis p = 1.59 × 10−20). (h) Top 10 genes ranked by SHAP values according to their contribution to PAAG. (i) Top 10 DNA methylation sites ranked by SHAP values according to their contribution to PAAG. (j) The biological processes (BP) significantly enriched in the top 100 SHAP‐prioritized RNA‐seq genes together with their correlated/co‐expressed genes.

ai.summary_zh: 该论文提出个性化情境感知年龄差(PAAG)指标,用于刻画衰老加速,并构建预训练模型 AOE-Net(Age Order Enhanced Network)。据摘要与图注,AOE-Net 在健康人群多组学数据上采用年龄顺序增强的对比学习,学习可重建衰老轨迹的潜在表征;PAAG 通过微调 AOE-Net 生成,并在泛癌总生存、亚临床动脉粥样硬化(PESA 评分)与骨质疏松(骨密度)等结局上与传统第一、二代衰老时钟的年龄差(AG)比较。图注还描述了在 TARGET 泛癌队列中的免疫相关分析及 SHAP 基因贡献与富集分析。作者代码未运行,静态检查不构成复现验证;输入尺度、图号与代码的对应关系等未明示信息保持未知。

图注显示预训练数据包括 GTEx 的非配对 RNA-seq 与 DNA 甲基化,以及 TCGA 正常样本的配对数据。
图 2 图注描述按 PAAG 分组的泛癌患者(减速、正常、加速)在年轻、中年、老年亚组中的 Kaplan–Meier 生存曲线,加速组总生存最差。
图 2 图注还描述将 PAAG 与 DeepMAge、BiT age clock、PhenoAge、horvathAge 等时钟在 HR 与 C-index 上比较,并含消融实验。
图 3 与图 4 图注描述基于 SHAP 的基因贡献排序与 GO 生物学过程富集,用于解释 PAAG 的分子驱动因素。

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling revealed seasonal shifts and age- associated changes in rhesus monkey testes. A Flowchart of the experimental design depicting testicular aging and reproductive seasons in rhesus monkeys. B Representative H&E staining of testicular sections across ages and seasons. Scale bars, 100 μm. C Oil Red O staining of testicular sections from prepuberty, adult and aged monkeys during the non-breeding (NB) and breeding (B) seasons. Upper panel: representative images; Lower panel: quantification of Oil Red O-positive area in NB and B samples, respectively, presented as fold changes. Data are shown as means ± SEM. Scale bars, 50 μm. D UMAP plot showing testicular cell types. Left panel: annotation of 14 distinct cell types in monkey testes. Right panel: distribution of different cell types across age and seasonal groups. E Dot plot showing cell type canonical marker gene expression. Dot size represents the proportion of cells expressing each gene; Color indicates average expression level. F Bar plots showing the proportions of germ cells (top) and somatic cells (bottom) across age and seasonal conditions. G The Sankey diagram (left) showing the flow from age and seasonal categories to specific cell types. Pie charts (right) summarize the proportional distribution of age and seasonal groups within each cell type.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Adult testicular meiosis in rhesus monkeys exhibits seasonal transcriptional oscillations aligned with the reproductive cycle. A Radar plot displaying the numbers of DEGs across cell types under different comparisons. Left panel: upregulated (left) and downregulated (right) DEGs in breeding season versus non-breeding season across age stages. Right panel: upregulated (left) and downregulated (right) DEGs during development and aging. The numerical labels indicate the scale of DEG counts. B Circular bar plots showing scaled expression of representative functional gene categories across cell types under indicated age or seasonal conditions. The length of each bar represents the scaled expression level. Arcs indicate functional gene categories, while inner ring indicates cell types. C UMAP plot illustrating the cell subtypes of spermatogenic cells. Upper panel: cell type annotation; lower panel: distribution across age groups and reproductive seasons. D Empirical Cumulative Distribution Function (ECDF) plot displaying the distribution of spermatogenic cells along pseudotime progression. Curves represent the cumulative proportion of cells reaching each pseudotime point under different age and seasonal conditions. E Immunofluorescence staining of seminiferous tubules showing DAPI (blue), DDX4 (green) and SYCP3 (red). Representative images are shown in the upper panels, and quantification (means ± SEM) is shown in the lower panels. Positive SYCP3 positive area is quantified as fold changes. Scale bars, 20 μm. F Line plot modules displaying the smoothed expression of key regulatory genes during meiosis along pseudotime (left panel), and their corresponding qPCR validation results (right panel). G GO terms enrichment analysis of DEGs in germ cell types. Orange indicates pathways upregulated in breeding versus non-breeding seasons in adults, whereas blue indicates pathways downregulated in aged versus adult. Dot size represents the number of genes assigned to each GO term. Color intensity indicates statistical significance, with p-values calculated using the hypergeometric distribution.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Sertoli cells regulate seasonal meiotic dynamics through tight junction-mediated blood-testis barrier remodeling. A Bubble heatmap showing ligand-receptor interaction pairs between Sertoli.a cells and meiosis germ cells across age and seasonal conditions. Dot color gradient reflects interaction strength. Network representations visualize enriched GO terms of significant interaction pairs in the non-breeding season (left, grey) and breeding season (right, light yellow). The accompanying protein-protein interaction (PPI) network visualizes the corresponding gene pairs identified in the bubble plot. Node color and size represent the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), reflecting the importance of each gene in the network. B GSEA showing enrichment of "regulation of cell substrate adhesion" in Sertoli. a cell (left) and "tight junction organization" in meiosis cells (right). Genes were ranked by log2(fold change) (breeding versus non-breeding seasons). C Dot plot displaying log2(fold change) (breeding versus non-breeding seasons) of representative genes associated with “tight junction organization” and “regulation of cell substrate adhesion” in Sertoli.a cells (top) and meiotic cells (bottom). Dot size indicates the number of genes contributing to each term; dot color indicates statistical significance. D Representative transmission electron microscopy images showing tight junction ultrastructure between adjacent Sertoli cells at the basal region of seminiferous tubule during the non-breeding and breeding seasons. Scale bars, 1 μm.

figures.label: FIGURE 1
figures.caption: Overlap among the results of DTU methods. (A) Workflow for measuring the overlap among DTU method results. Transcript expression data under different conditions are used as input for ten representative DTU methods. Each method produces a ranked list of significant transcripts. For any two methods, we rank transcripts by significance, select the top transcripts from each list, and calculate their overlap using the Jaccard index. (B) Quantitative comparison of overlaps among DTU method results across datasets. Different box colors represent different data types, including RBP KO/KD short‐read bulk RNA‐seq data, as well as long‐read bulk RNA‐seq, long‐read single‐cell RNA‐seq, and long‐read spatial RNA‐seq data without KO/KD. Each data type contains several datasets; for example, the long‐read spatial type includes CBS1, CBS2, and MOB. Each dataset includes multiple biological conditions (for example, different spatial regions), which are paired to form condition pairs. Each point in the boxplot represents the Jaccard index between two DTU methods under one condition pair at a given top threshold. The x‐axis shows the top thresholds based on significance in DTU results, and the y‐axis shows the Jaccard index of significant transcripts between two methods.

figures.label: FIGURE 2
figures.caption: Framework for evaluating DTU methods. (A) Collection of datasets and DTU methods. It includes short‐read bulk RNA‐seq datasets from RBP KO/KD experiments, as well as long‐read bulk RNA‐seq, long‐read single‐cell RNA‐seq, and long‐read spatial RNA‐seq datasets without KO/KD. Ten representative DTU methods are evaluated. (B) Construction of a reference transcript set based on real biological data. It includes the common transcript set (left panel), the regulated transcript set (right panel), and the overlapped transcript set (middle panel). (C) Design of a DTU‐specific evaluation metric. The transcript set enrichment score (TSES) is designed to evaluate the enrichment of the reference transcript set along a transcript list ranked by P‐value in a DTU result. The score is then normalized using random permutations.

figures.label: FIGURE 3
figures.caption: Quantitative validation of reference transcript sets. The reliability of the common, regulated, and overlapped transcript sets is tested by comparing transcripts within and outside each reference set in RBP KO/KD datasets. (A) Workflow for evaluating reference transcript sets. The common transcript set, regulated transcript set, and overlapped transcript set are compared with transcripts outside the corresponding set. The comparison is based on expression proportion fold changes between RBP KO/KD and control groups and binding signals. (B) Statistical validation of common, regulated, and overlapped transcript sets. In each boxplot, colored boxes represent transcripts within the corresponding set, while grey boxes represent transcripts outside the set. The y‐axis represents RBP KO/KD datasets, and the x‐axis shows expression proportion fold change or binding signal. Annotation bars indicate experimental technology, cell line, RBP Function, and Significance from t‐test and rank‐sum test. (C) Effect size of expression proportion fold change and binding signal. Effect size is calculated as median (within) minus median (outside) for each RBP KO/KD dataset and each reference transcript set. Boxplots summarize effect size values, and the scatter plot shows the relationship between the effect size of expression proportion fold change and the effect size of binding signal.

A Real-Data-Driven Framework for Evaluating Differential Transcript Usage Methods Across Long-Read Bulk, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomics.. DOI: 10.1002/advs.77756. Source: NLM PMC OA Cloud. License: CC BY.

figures.label: FIGURE 4
figures.caption: Quantification of unbiasedness, stability, and effectiveness of evaluation metrics. (A) Schematic overview of how unbiasedness, stability, and effectiveness are quantified. Unbiasedness is defined as one minus the correlation between the number of significant transcripts predicted by each DTU method and its accuracy score. Stability measures the correlation of scores for the same DTU method across different datasets. Effectiveness evaluates how well a metric distinguishes real accuracy from random noise by comparing real scores with those from random permutations. (B) Quantitative comparison of unbiasedness, stability, and effectiveness across different evaluation metrics. The left panel shows a 3D plot, where the x‐, y‐, and z‐axes represent unbiasedness, stability, and effectiveness, respectively. Each point indicates the scores of these three metrics under a specific combination of reference transcript set and evaluation metric. The middle panel displays an annotation bar showing the combination of each reference transcript set with its corresponding evaluation metric. The right panel presents the detailed scores of unbiasedness, stability, and effectiveness for each combination, together with the overall score, calculated as the average of the three. The upper and lower sections represent RNA‐seq data from different experimental conditions, including RBP knockout or knockdown (KO/KD) data and non‐KO/KD data.

figures.caption: Evaluation results of ten representative DTU methods. (A) TSES of different DTU methods across multiple datasets. The y‐axis represents the TSES values, and the x‐axis shows the DTU methods. Each dot in the boxplot indicates the TSES value of one condition pair within a dataset. Methods on the x‐axis are ranked by their mean TSES values. (B) Ranking of DTU methods based on TSES in different datasets. In the radar chart, a point further away from the center indicates a higher ranking of the corresponding method in that dataset.

figures.label: FIGURE 6
figures.caption: Parameter sensitivity analysis of the evaluation framework. (A) Similarity in the accuracy of different models for predicting regulated transcripts. The yellow box represents the generalized linear model, and the black box represents linear discriminant analysis. The y‐axis shows accuracy metrics; the four boxplots on the left use area under the precision‐recall curve (AUPRC), and the four on the right use area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Statistical significance is tested using a paired t‐test. (B) Similarity of TSES scores based on reference transcript sets obtained from different prediction models. The x‐axis shows TSES values calculated from reference transcript sets predicted by the generalized linear model (GLM), and the y‐axis shows those predicted by linear discriminant analysis (LDA). Similarity is measured using Spearman correlation and its significance. Different colors represent different data types: dark red for long‐read bulk RNA‐seq data, dark green for long‐read single‐cell RNA‐seq data, and dark blue for long‐read spatial RNA‐seq data. (C) Effect of the parameter α in the TSES metric. The left panel shows a 3D plot of unbiasedness, stability, and effectiveness for different α values (0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 10), while the right panel presents the corresponding numerical scores. figures.caption: Workflow and validation of RBP activity prediction using DTU‐, DTE‐, and DGE‐based rankings. (A) Workflow of RBP activity prediction. ai.title_zh: 面向长读长批量、单细胞与空间转录组的真实数据驱动差异转录本使用评估框架
ai.summary_zh: 该论文提出一个基于真实数据的差异转录本使用(DTU)方法评估框架,覆盖长读长批量、单细胞和空间转录组数据。框架包含两部分:一是利用 RBP 敲除/敲低 RNA-seq 数据与实验验证的 RBP-转录本互作构建有生物学依据的参考转录本集;二是提出 DTU 专用指标——转录本集富集分数(TSES),用于量化方法在排序结果中对参考转录本的优先程度。文中称该框架在多个真实 RNA-seq 数据集上从可靠性、无偏性、稳定性、有效性和稳健性方面进行验证,并据此评估十种代表性 DTU 方法,还扩展到预测转录本水平的 RBP 活性。上述内容均来自摘要与图注描述,作者代码未运行,未做复现验证。

figures.label: FIGURE 1
figures.caption: Overview of the MAPA framework. (a) MAPA takes transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic features as input and performs pathway enrichment analysis to obtain pathway‐level functional information. (b) MAPA constructs a network connecting molecules and pathways and discovers the functional modules. (c) MAPA generates LLM‐assisted function interpretation using module components, experimental information, and related literature, and provides multiple visualizations to support module interpretation.

figures.label: FIGURE 2
figures.caption: Evaluation of MAPA's core methodological components. (a) Workflow for constructing the curated pathway dataset. (b) Pairwise within‐module (n = 92) and between‐module (n = 854) pathway similarities calculated using biotext embedding, Jaccard index, and overlap coefficient. (c) Case study of one representative module containing three functionally related entries. (d) Gene set overlap among the three entries shown in c. (e) Pairwise similarity among the three entries calculated using biotext embedding, Jaccard index, overlap coefficient, and Wang semantic similarity, where applicable. (f) Workflow for evaluating MAPA‐generated functional interpretation using human expert annotations and size‐matched random modules as negative controls. (g) Pairwise inter‐expert similarities of functional interpretations for each module (n = 10 comparisons per module). (h) Principal‐component analysis (PCA) of module interpretation generated by human experts (circles) and MAPA (triangles). (i) Comparison of intra‐module biotext embedding similarity between real and size‐matched random modules, based on all pathway pairs within each module (n = 3 for Modules 4, 5, and 7; n = 21 for Modules 8–10; n = 10 for Modules 11 and 12, per group). (j) Comparison of MAPA confidence scores for the same real and random modules (n = 8 per group). For b, g, i, and j, center lines indicate medians, boxes indicate the interquartile range (IQR), and whiskers extend to the most extreme values within 1.5 × IQR. For b, i, and j, statistical significance was assessed using Wilcoxon rank‐sum tests. *** p‐value < 0.001, ** p‐value < 0.01, * p‐value < 0.05.

figures.caption: Benchmarking MAPA against existing approaches for functional module discovery and interpretation. (a) Workflow for benchmarking functional module discovery. figures.caption: MAPA identifies coordinated aging‐related functional dysregulation across omics datasets. (c) Networks of shared functional modules between the parietal lobe and duodenum, highlighting cross‐tissue coordination along the brain‐gut axis. ai.title_zh: MAPA:面向多组学数据功能模块发现与解释的语义网络框架
ai.summary_zh: 该资料介绍 MAPA(Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using LLMs),一个用于多组学数据功能模块发现与解释的语义-生物网络框架。据摘要与图注,MAPA 将转录组、蛋白质组和代谢组特征作为输入,先做通路富集获得通路层面功能信息,再构建连接分子与通路的网络以发现功能模块,并借助大语言模型与检索增强生成(RAG)结合模块组分、实验信息和相关文献生成结构化解释,同时提供多种可视化。图注还描述了方法学评估(模块内/间通路相似性、专家注释对比、随机模块阴性对照)以及与现有方法的基准比较(Jaccard 指数、ARI、文本嵌入余弦相似度、Wilcoxon 检验)和衰老相关多组学案例。作者代码未执行,输入尺度与图号对应关系未明示处保持未知。
learning_points: MAPA 的流程分三步:多组学特征输入与通路富集、分子-通路网络构建与功能模块发现、LLM 辅助的功能解释与可视化(据 FIGURE 1 图注)。
框架使用随机游走重启(random walk with restart)量化分子与通路之间的全局功能相关性,以支持跨组学层的一致模块发现(据摘要)。
解释环节结合大语言模型与检索增强生成(RAG),输入包括模块组分、实验信息和相关文献(据摘要与 FIGURE 1 图注)。
方法学评估包含模块内与模块间通路相似性计算,使用 biotext embedding、Jaccard 指数、重叠系数,并在适用时使用 Wang 语义相似度(据 FIGURE 2 图注)。
解释质量评估采用人类专家注释与规模匹配的随机模块作为阴性对照,并以主成分分析展示专家与 MAPA 解释的分布(据 FIGURE 2 图注)。
基准比较中,模块发现以 Jaccard 指数热图与 ARI 汇总与真值模块的一致性;解释质量以文本嵌入余弦相似度衡量,并用 Wilcoxon 秩和检验做统计比较(据 FIGURE 3 图注)。
案例部分展示衰老相关多组学数据中的共享功能模块网络,包括脑区之间及脑-肠轴跨组织协调,以及血浆蛋白模块(据 FIGURE 4 图注)。
代码静态观察显示可视化脚本涉及读取 enriched_functional_module.rda 等数据对象,但未运行,不能据此推断复现结果(据 script-1、script-2)。

ai.title_zh: 雌性冈比亚按蚊脑的空间与单细胞分辨率图谱
ai.summary_zh: 该研究以雌性冈比亚按蚊(Anopheles gambiae)脑为对象,结合单细胞转录组与空间转录组,刻画其细胞多样性与空间组织,并与其他昆虫物种进行比较;同时利用单脑与单细胞 RNA 测序描述与蚊虫生活史事件相关的转录变化。摘要指出未发现特定细胞群扩张,而观察到交配后神经传递的调节、吸血后与胶质细胞、Kenyon 细胞和免疫细胞相关的代谢与免疫反应,以及脑内衰老特征;未发现恶性疟原虫(Plasmodium falciparum)感染的影响。图注显示单细胞图谱包含 48,806 个高质量单细胞转录组、45 个簇,空间数据包含 9,914 个高质量空间转录组。作者代码未执行,本条目仅为基于图注与静态信息的待核学习注释。
learning_points: 图注显示单细胞图谱基于 48,806 个高质量单细胞转录组,来自三种实验条件、每种两个实验重复共六个样本,每个样本取自十只脑。
图注显示图谱划分为 45 个簇,并用 elav-like、repo、col4a 等标记基因展示神经元、胶质与免疫细胞相关表达。
图注显示将冈比亚按蚊簇与埃及伊蚊、黑腹果蝇、法老蚁和意大利蜜蜂的细胞类型进行比对,并以 >0.4 的对齐值加星号标注。
图注显示空间部分包含 9,914 个高质量空间转录组,并在五个高质量对齐的头部区域中展示簇的空间位置。
图注显示对胶质细胞类型做了细分,涉及通用胶质标记 repo、thr3DH,表面胶质标记 tret1 与神经毡相关胶质标记 scmt1。

摘要报告交配后神经传递调节、吸血后胶质细胞/Kenyon 细胞/免疫细胞的代谢与免疫反应,以及衰老特征,未发现疟原虫感染效应。

ai.title_zh: 评估不同比对工具对法医表观遗传时钟准确性的影响
ai.summary_zh: 该研究将一套成熟法医表观遗传时钟产生的数据,分别用四种亚硫酸氢盐专用比对工具(Bwa-meth、Abismal、Bismark、BS-Seeker2)进行比对,每个工具测试最多六种参数设置,考察最终预测年龄是否因工具与设置不同而出现明显差异,并评估读深、精确率、召回率、F1 与比对运行时间等质控指标。摘要称 Abismal、Bismark、BS-Seeker2 的测试设置均未在年龄预测准确性上超过原用工具 Bwa-meth,但不同工具间最终年龄预测存在差异;研究还开发了 Shiny 应用 MethylAge Explorer。图 1 展示 10 种比对设置的年龄预测结果(含等值线与趋势线),图 2 以小提琴图展示各设置间 beta 值的一致性,并标出用于血液年龄预测的六个目标 CpG 位点。

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Serval MERlin decoding workflow. Serval’s MERlin pipeline comprises six sequential modules: (A) chromatic correction to remove inter-channel misalignment; (B) fiducial alignment for sub-pixel registration across imaging rounds; (C) image transformations (background subtraction, denoising, deconvolution); (D) decoding of pixel intensities into barcode identities; (E) filtering of low-confidence or off-target barcodes; and (F) export of the final barcode table for downstream single-cell analysis.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: CoSiD matches MERlin performance and exceeds competing decoding methods in synthetic benchmarks. (A) Exact recall across the ten simulation scenarios defined in Table S1. (B) Exact false discovery rate (FDR). (C) Exact F1 score. (D) Maximum Pearson correlation coefficient between decoded and ground-truth transcript abundances. Points represent the mean across 100 replicates per scenario and error bars indicate the standard error of the mean. Lines connect each decoder across scenarios to aid visual tracking of performance and do not imply continuity or ordering between scenarios. (D) UMAP visualization of CoSiD vs MERlin decoded 4T1 tissue, coloured by scGate annotation. ’Unknown’ (dark grey) denotes cells lacking sufficient marker signal to pass any gate; ’Multi’ (light grey) denotes cells with detectable but conflicting lineage signatures. High-confidence cells were defined as cells receiving concordant labels from scGate marker gating and Seurat label transfer to the snRNA-seq reference. Cells are shown by unsupervised cluster identity and by predicted major class annotation, highlighting improved clustering stability after CoSiD. (F) Spatial organization of SpaMask domains across the full CoSiD-decoded dataset. (G) Comparison of transcript recovery for selected marker genes between RNAscope, DART-FISH SpD, and CoSiD, reproducing the DART-FISH paper benchmarking analysis. ai.summary_zh: 该文献提出 Serval 模块化解码框架,将解码流程拆分为可独立配置的模块,并据此开发 CoSiD(余弦相似度解码器)。作者在合成与真实 MERFISH 数据上比较 CoSiD 与基线方法,并扩展到 DART-FISH 平台。图注显示 Serval 的 MERlin 流程包含六个顺序模块,CoSiD 在合成基准中与 MERlin 表现相当并超过其他竞争方法,在 4T1 MERFISH 与 DART-FISH 数据上改善转录本恢复与聚类/注释可解释性。作者代码未执行,本文仅为基于图注与摘要的静态学习注释,未验证复现结果。
learning_points: Serval 将解码流程拆分为可独立配置的模块,便于替换与组合不同算法(依据摘要与 Figure 1 图注)。
Figure 1 图注列出 MERlin 流程的六个顺序模块:色差校正、基准点对齐、图像变换、像素强度解码为条形码、低置信/脱靶条形码过滤、导出条形码表。
CoSiD 通过优化与已知条形码的余弦相似度来改进转录本恢复(依据摘要)。
Figure 2 图注显示合成基准包含十个模拟场景,评估指标为精确召回率、精确 FDR、精确 F1 与解码丰度与真值的最大 Pearson 相关系数,每场景 100 次重复并给出均值与标准误。
Figure 3 图注显示在 4T1 细胞培养与组织 MERFISH 数据上比较六种解码方法,并展示脱靶标志基因/空白点图、空间注释、UMAP 与近似轮廓宽度。
Figure 4 图注显示 CoSiD 扩展到 DART-FISH 数据,展示高置信细胞 UMAP、聚类注释、兴奋性神经元亚类拆分、皮层深度空间定位与 SpaMask 层组成。
静态检查仅观察到脚本读取 CSV 与 codebook 的列选择等片段,未运行代码,不能据此推断完整数据结构或复现结论。

figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.caption: crumblr analysis workflow.A crumblr transformation of the count matrix enables precision weighting for variance partition analysis, linear mixed model testing for differential cell frequency, and multivariate testing along a cellular hierarchy. B Standard deviation of the CLR-transformed proportions from 1000 samples drawn from a Dirichlet-multinomial distribution (blue points) is compared to the normal approximation developed here (red line) when at least two counts are observed. Data was simulated using an overdispersion of τ = 10, 500 total counts across 15 categories and 1000 simulations. C Illustration showing the estimated coefficient estimated using standard regression fit on CLR-transformed proportions (blue line), and precision-weighted regression using crumblr (red line) that models the measurement uncertainty in the count ratios, shown here by error bars indicating 95% confidence intervals. D Multivariate hypothesis testing in crumblr enables analysis of internal nodes in a hierarchical clustering of cell types while modeling estimated effect sizes and the correlation between them.
